headline_marked: Jamaat-e-Islami's [[Benazir Ahmed's arrest is Interpol's credit]], not government's
headline: Jamaat-e-Islami's Benazir Ahmed's arrest is Interpol's credit, not government's
summary: Opposition leader Shafiqur Rahman says the current government did not issue the Red Notice for the former IGP, attributing the arrest in Dubai to Interpol's efforts.
details: Jamaat-e-Islami's Amir and opposition leader Shafiqur Rahman stated that the current government deserves no credit for the arrest of former Inspector General of Police (IGP) Benazir Ahmed in Dubai.
Speaking to journalists at the Sylhet Circuit House, Rahman claimed that the Red Notice for Benazir Ahmed was not issued by the current administration, but by the previous government.
He described the arrest as an achievement for Bangladesh, but noted that whether Benazir is brought back to the country depends on the government's will.
Beyond the arrest, Rahman criticized the Indian Embassy's reaction to requests for explanations regarding the newly appointed Indian Ambassador's remarks.
He also condemned a BNP member of parliament's remarks about the dress of female opposition members, calling for the same level of respect and patriotism in Parliament.
Rahman emphasized that the opposition will maintain a moderate path in Parliament, but warned that street protests will continue if solutions are not found within the legislative body.
He further claimed that the current government has ignored the 'July Charter' and the mandate of the people's referendum, risking national stability.
caption:
Was the arrest of former IGP Benazir Ahmed a government win? Jamaat's Amir says no.

Jamaat-e-Islami's Amir and opposition leader Shafiqur Rahman stated that the current government deserves no credit for the arrest of former Inspector General of Police (IGP) Benazir Ahmed in Dubai.

Speaking to journalists at the Sylhet Circuit House, Rahman claimed that the Red Notice for Benazir Ahmed was not issued by the current administration, but by the previous government.

He described the arrest as an achievement for Bangladesh, but noted that whether Benazir is brought back to the country depends on the government's will.

Beyond the arrest, Rahman criticized the Indian Embassy's reaction to requests for explanations regarding the newly appointed Indian Ambassador's remarks.

He also condemned a BNP member of parliament's remarks about the dress of female opposition members, calling for the same level of respect and patriotism in Parliament.

Rahman emphasized that the opposition will maintain a moderate path in Parliament, but warned that street protests will continue if solutions are not found within the legislative body.

He further claimed that the current government has ignored the 'July Charter' and the mandate of the people's referendum, risking national stability.

Source: Prothom Alo, Dhaka Tribune, Somoy News, bdnews24.com, Jamuna TV

headline_marked: India rejects Nepal's bid to [[add 20MW power exports to Bangladesh]]
headline: India rejects Nepal's bid to add 20MW power exports to Bangladesh
summary: India's Central Electricity Authority has cited transmission constraints, stalling Nepal's plan to increase its electricity supply to Bangladesh to 60MW.
details: India has declined approval for an additional 20MW of electricity exports from Nepal to Bangladesh, citing constraints on cross-border transmission capacity.
The decision by India’s Central Electricity Authority (CEA) means that only the existing 40MW framework will be operational for now.
Nepal exports surplus hydropower during the wet monsoon season and imports power from India during the winter months.
A bilateral meeting in Dhaka on November 27, 2025, had previously agreed in principle to scale up the trade to 60MW.
The Nepal Electricity Authority (NEA) approached India's NVVN for clearance, but was notified that the 1,000MW India–Bangladesh grid corridor could not absorb the extra load.
The electricity travels from Nepal's Dhalkebar to Muzaffarpur in India, then enters Bangladesh through the Baharampur–Bheramara grid link.
The current 40MW supply is sourced from the Trishuli and Chilime hydropower stations at a tariff of 6.40 US cents per unit.
Nepal currently holds aggregate approvals to export 1,165MW of electricity combined to India and Bangladesh.
caption:
India has blocked Nepal's plan to increase electricity exports to Bangladesh, citing grid capacity issues.

India has declined approval for an additional 20MW of electricity exports from Nepal to Bangladesh, citing constraints on cross-border transmission capacity.

The decision by India’s Central Electricity Authority (CEA) means that only the existing 40MW framework will be operational for now.

Nepal exports surplus hydropower during the wet monsoon season and imports power from India during the winter months.

A bilateral meeting in Dhaka on November 27, 2025, had previously agreed in principle to scale up the trade to 60MW.

The Nepal Electricity Authority (NEA) approached India's NVVN for clearance, but was notified that the 1,000MW India–Bangladesh grid corridor could not absorb the extra load.

The electricity travels from Nepal's Dhalkebar to Muzaffarpur in India, then enters Bangladesh through the Baharampur–Bheramara grid link.

The current 40MW supply is sourced from the Trishuli and Chilime hydropower stations at a tariff of 6.40 US cents per unit.

Nepal currently holds aggregate approvals to export 1,165MW of electricity combined to India and Bangladesh.
